item.title: Football robots
item.description: Two attacking robots and a goalkeeper that moves, five fixed spots, fifteen seconds each, and at least one pass before any shot. We wrote the tactics as Lua state machines and our own C++ skill DLLs, scoring 80 points without a single foul in the national qualifier.

item.title: MachiKoro board game in C++
item.description: A dice-driven board game in C++14 for 1-N players and AI: 15 buildings, 4 landmarks, five-colour card settlement, market purchases and win conditions.

item.title: Punch-list tracking and assisted localisation on site
item.description: Supported MOEX/OPC on the Cœur Défense office refurbishment (floors 34–39): site inspections, access and logistics coordination, punch-list tracking in IDCapture, and OpenCV experiments for locating ceiling openings and missing sprinkler rosettes.

item.title: The Podcast of Engineers
item.description: A trilingual engineer interview podcast run with friends from UTSEUS — 14 episodes and 14 guests from academia and industry, from Meituan, Microsoft and Google to the former president of École Centrale de Lyon.

item.title: BEST: multi-scale territorial balance and urban well-being
item.description: Contributed to the BEST project at UTC’s Avenues laboratory: three PRISMA systematic reviews (560 articles), two indicator frameworks for territorial systems and well-being, an OECD correlation analysis, and a multi-scale conceptual framework supported by Vensim and ArcGIS.

item.title: Photovoltaic MPPT — P&O and its improved variant
item.description: Modelled a Kyocera KC200GT module in MATLAB/Simulink and compared P&O against the improved P&OA over 366 days of per-minute irradiance and temperature measured by UTC’s STELLA platform, in terms of annual energy and efficiency.

item.title: Smart delivery drone
item.description: Autonomously crossing obstacles, recognising patterns and making three pinpoint drops inside a 4 × 4 m arena. PX4 plus a Jetson Nano, with a ROS state machine driving take-off, cruise, descent and release.

item.title: TZ: Science communication as method
item.description: Final-year project “Développement méthodologique par la médiation scientifique” — a PRISMA-style review (183→67 references), one classroom field observation and a four-step methodological framework arguing that science mediation can be the research protocol itself, not just downstream dissemination.

item.title: PhD proposal SOUND: access ergonomics for electric mobility in cross-border territories
item.description: The SOUND doctoral proposal asks whether the electric mobility transition narrows or widens inequalities of access in European cross-border territories marked by institutional and energy discontinuities — three hypotheses, a four-phase 36-month plan, and 32 days a year of science mediation built into the method.

item.title: Unity game development learning portfolio
item.description: Four Unity prototypes (rolling-ball arcade, dragon shooter, colour runner, character movement) and eight C# console exercises, covering Rigidbody physics, collisions and triggers, UGUI, scene management, coroutines, Animator, particles and audio. Three Windows builds are available from GitHub Releases.

item.title: Gopher & Dodo hex-board game AI
item.description: An AI for Mark Steere’s two-player hex games Gopher and Dodo: axial-coordinate board, legal-move generation, a mobility evaluation and memoised Minimax search.

item.title: Bordeaux Airbnb price prediction
item.description: An end-to-end study of 11,854 Bordeaux listings from Inside Airbnb: EDA, maps and ANOVA, five features mined from the listing title, and a 100 € price split comparing linear regression, random forest, Ridge and Lasso. Random forest reaches a test R² of 0.52 (low price) and 0.55 (high price).

item.title: Dunkirk heatwave sensitivity
item.description: An ArcGIS study that decomposes ‘why cities heat up’ into three continuous fields — building heat, vegetation cooling and water cooling — combines them with two-pass kernel density and multi-criteria weighting, and produces a heatwave sensitivity index for Dunkirk. The building effect is about 3.3× vegetation and 55× water.

item.title: Vehicle-sharing platform database (UTC-NF18)
item.description: Designed the vehicleShare platform from requirements and UML to a PostgreSQL implementation: 18 tables, integrity constraints, a Python/psycopg2 command-line application, and a NoSQL variant storing insurance, invoices and reviews in JSON columns.

item.title: Dual-motor distributed drive and electronic differential
item.description: Replacing the mechanical differential with two independently driven rear wheels: an Arduino Uno + L298N + two TT motors model car, a pygame animation of the inner/outer wheel speed difference, and the competition paper, technical route and a Keras regression example.

item.title: Gram–Schmidt orthogonalisation: a numerical comparison
item.description: Implemented classical Gram–Schmidt (CGS) and the modified version (MGS) in MATLAB and C, compared the two orthonormal bases in Frobenius norm on ill-conditioned matrices and 100 random 100×100 matrices, and explained why formulas that are equivalent on paper separate in floating point.

item.title: Data structures: C++ templates and course labs
item.description: Organised seven chapters of course work into 36 topic modules and two integrative projects: C++ templates for lists, stacks, queues, trees and graphs, covering KMP, Huffman, union-find, minimum spanning trees, shortest paths, topological sort and critical paths.
